bullet_points: In the second quarter of fiscal 2O26, we benefited from a \$180 millon release of previously reserved H20 inventory related to the sale of approximately \$650 million of H20 to an unrestricted customer outside of China. There were no H20 sales to China-based customers in the second quarter.

GAAP gross margin was 72.4%,and GAAP diluted earnings per share was \$1.08, for the quarter. Excluding the \$180 milion release and related tax impact, non-GAAP gross margin for the quarter would have been 72.3% and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share would have been \$1.04.
Revenue for the second quarter was \$46.7 bilion,up 56% from a year ago and up 6% sequentially.

Data Center revenue for the second quarter was \$41.1 bilion, up 56% from a year ago and up 5% sequentially. The strong_year-on-year and sequential growth was driven by demand for our accelerated computing platform used for large language models，recommendation engines,and generative and agentic Al applications. We continue to ramp our Blackwell architecture, which grew 17% sequentially，including our newest architecture， Blackwell UItra.We recognized Blackwell revenue across all customer categories, led by large cloud service providers，which represented approximately 5O% of Data Center revenue.

Data Center compute revenue was \$33.8 bilion, up 50% from a year ago. Sequentially，compute revenue declined 1%, driven by a \$4.0 bilion reduction in H2O sales.Networking revenue was \$7.3 billion，up 98% from a year ago and up 46% sequentially,driven by the growth of NVLink compute fabric for GB2OO and GB300 systems， the ramp of XDR InfiniBand products，and adoption of Ethernet for Al solutions at cloud service providers and consumer internet companies.
Gaming revenue for the second quarter was up 49% from a year ago and up 14% sequentially,with strong sales and increased supply of our Blackwell product.

Professional Visualization revenue for the second quarter was up 32% from a year ago and up 18% sequentially，driven by the acceleration of Blackwell sales in our Notebook products,addressing Al workflows, real-time graphics rendering and data simulation.
Automotive revenue for the second quarter was up 69% from a year ago and up 3% sequentially, driven by strong adoption of our self-driving platforms.

GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins for the second quarter decreased from a year ago as our Blackwell revenue consists primarily of ful-scale datacenter systems compared to Hopper HGX systems last year. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins increased sequentially as the prior quarter included a \$4.5 bilion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations.

GAAP operating expenses for the second quarter were up 38% from a year ago and up 8% sequentially,and non-GAAP operating expenses were up 36% from a year ago and up 6% sequentialy. The increases were primarily driven by compute and infrastructure costs and higher compensation and benefits due to compensation increases and employee growth.

Interest income for the second quarter was \$592 million,up from a year ago and sequentially, reflecting growth in cash,cash equivalents,and debt securities. Net other income for the second quarter was \$2.2 bilion, primarily driven by gains in a publicly-held equity security.

Cash,cash equivalents and marketable securities were \$56.8 billon,up from \$34.8 billion a year ago and \$53.7 billion a quarter ago. The increases primarily reflect higher revenue，partially offset by stock repurchases.
Accounts_receivable was_\$27.8 billion_ with 54 days sales_outstanding (DSO)， up from 46 days sequentially,driven by timing of cash collections and Blackwell Ultra ramping late in the quarter.
nventory was \$15.0 billion, up from \$11.3 billon sequentially,to support the rampof Blackwell UItra.

Total purchase commitments were \$45.8 bilion,comprised of inventory,manufacturing capacity,and non-inventory purchase obligations,up from \$43.5 bilion sequentially,on additional multi-year cloud service agreements to support our research and development efforts.

Cash flow from operating activities was \$15.4 bilion, up from \$14.5 billon a year ago and down from \$27.4 billion a quarter ago.The year-on-year increase reflects growth in revenue,partially offset by an increase in working capital.The sequential decrease was mainly driven by \$8.1 billion in taxes paid in the quarter.
We returned \$10.O billion to shareholders in the second quarter through \$9.7 billion of share repurchases and \$244 million of cash dividends.

technology_highlights: Data Center revenue for the second quarter was \$41.1 bilion, up 56% from a year ago and up 5% sequentially. The strong_year-on-year and sequential growth was driven by demand for our accelerated computing platform used for large language models，recommendation engines,and generative and agentic Al applications. We continue to ramp our Blackwell architecture, which grew 17% sequentially，including our newest architecture， Blackwell UItra.We recognized Blackwell revenue across all customer categories, led by large cloud service providers，which represented approximately 5O% of Data Center revenue.

Data Center compute revenue was \$33.8 bilion, up 50% from a year ago. Sequentially，compute revenue declined 1%, driven by a \$4.0 bilion reduction in H2O sales.Networking revenue was \$7.3 billion，up 98% from a year ago and up 46% sequentially,driven by the growth of NVLink compute fabric for GB2OO and GB300 systems， the ramp of XDR InfiniBand products，and adoption of Ethernet for Al solutions at cloud service providers and consumer internet companies.
Gaming revenue for the second quarter was up 49% from a year ago and up 14% sequentially,with strong sales and increased supply of our Blackwell product.

Professional Visualization revenue for the second quarter was up 32% from a year ago and up 18% sequentially，driven by the acceleration of Blackwell sales in our Notebook products,addressing Al workflows, real-time graphics rendering and data simulation.
Automotive revenue for the second quarter was up 69% from a year ago and up 3% sequentially, driven by strong adoption of our self-driving platforms.

GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins for the second quarter decreased from a year ago as our Blackwell revenue consists primarily of ful-scale datacenter systems compared to Hopper HGX systems last year. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins increased sequentially as the prior quarter included a \$4.5 bilion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations.

GAAP operating expenses for the second quarter were up 38% from a year ago and up 8% sequentially,and non-GAAP operating expenses were up 36% from a year ago and up 6% sequentialy. The increases were primarily driven by compute and infrastructure costs and higher compensation and benefits due to compensation increases and employee growth.

Interest income for the second quarter was \$592 million,up from a year ago and sequentially, reflecting growth in cash,cash equivalents,and debt securities. Net other income for the second quarter was \$2.2 bilion, primarily driven by gains in a publicly-held equity security.
Accounts_receivable was_\$27.8 billion_ with 54 days sales_outstanding (DSO)， up from 46 days sequentially,driven by timing of cash collections and Blackwell Ultra ramping late in the quarter.
nventory was \$15.0 billion, up from \$11.3 billon sequentially,to support the rampof Blackwell UItra.

Cash flow from operating activities was \$15.4 bilion, up from \$14.5 billon a year ago and down from \$27.4 billion a quarter ago.The year-on-year increase reflects growth in revenue,partially offset by an increase in working capital.The sequential decrease was mainly driven by \$8.1 billion in taxes paid in the quarter.

bullet_points: Revenue for the third quarter was a record \$57.0 billon, up 62% from a year ago and up 22% sequentially.

Data Center revenue for the third quarter was a record \$51.2 bilion, up 66% from a year ago and up 25% sequentially,driven by three platform shifts - accelerated computing, powerful Al models,and agentic applications. Blackwel UItra is now our leading architecture across all customer categories while our prior Blackwellarchitecture saw continued strong demand. H2O sales were insignificant in the third quarter.

Data Center compute revenue was a record \$43.0 billion, up 56% from a year ago and up 27% sequentially. Networking revenue was a record \$8.2 bilion,up l62% from a year ago from the introduction and continued growth of NVLink compute fabric for GB2O0 and GB3OO systems. Networking revenue was up 13% sequentialy， driven by the growth of XDR InfiniBand products, NVLinkTM，and Ethernet for Al solutions，while shipment timing and supply availability varied compared to the prior quarter.

Gaming revenue for the third quarter was up 3O% from a year ago on the continued demand for Blackwell. Gaming revenue was down 1% sequentially as channel inventories have reached more normalized levels heading into the holiday season.
Professional Visualization revenue for the third quarter was up 56% from a year ago and up 26% sequentially,driven by the launch of our new DGX SparkTM as well as the growth of Blackwell sales.
Automotive revenue for the third quarter was up 32% from a year ago and up 1% sequentially,driven by continued adoption of our self-driving platforms.

GAAP operating expenses for the third quarter were up 36% from a year ago and up 8% sequentially, and non-GAAP operating expenses were up 38% from a year ago and up 11% sequentially. The increases were primarily driven by compute and infrastructure costs， higher compensation and benefits due to compensation increases and employee growth and engineering development costs for new product introductions.

Interest income for the third quarter was \$624 milion,up from a year ago and sequentially, reflecting growth in cash,cash equivalents,and debt securities.Net other income for the third quarter was \$1.4 billion,primarily driven by gains in non-marketable and publicly-held equity securities.

Cash,cash equivalents and marketable securities were \$60.6 billon,up from \$38.5 billion a year ago and \$56.8 billion a quarter ago. The increases primarily reflect higher revenue，partially offset by stock repurchases.
Accounts receivable was \$33.4 bilion with 53 days sales outstanding (DSO), down from 54 days sequentially, driven by timing of cash collections.

Inventory was \$19.8 billion,up from \$15.0 billon sequentilly,and total supply-related commitments were \$50.3 billion.We are ordering to secure long lead-time components,meet the demand for Blackwell,and support future architecture ramps.
Multi-year cloud service agreements were \$26.0 billion, up from \$12.6 billon sequentialy, to support our research and development efforts and DGXTM Cloud offerings.
Cash flow from operating activities was \$23.8 billon,up from \$17.6 billion a year ago and up from \$15.4 billion a quarter ago.The year-on-year and sequentialincreases reflect growth in revenue.
We returned \$12.7 billion to shareholders in the third quarter through \$12.5 billion of share repurchases and \$243 million of cash dividends.

gross_margin.description:
This is a financial table that presents a forecast for the fourth quarter of 2026 (Q4 T1 2026) in millions of dollars. The table breaks down gross margins and operating expenses under both GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) and non-GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles excluding certain items) standards.

### 1. Type of Chart/Visualization:
The visualization is a tabular format, which organizes financial data into categories and subcategories for easy comparison and analysis.

### 2. Metrics/Data Shown:
- **GAAP Gross Margin**: The percentage of revenue remaining after deducting cost of goods sold.
- **Impact of stock-based compensation expense, acquisition-related costs, and other costs**: Adjustments to the gross margin due to specific non-recurring expenses.
- **Non-GAAP Gross Margin**: The adjusted gross margin after excluding the specified impacts.
- **GAAP Operating Expenses**: Total operating expenses as per GAAP.
- **Stock-based compensation expense, acquisition-related costs, and other costs**: Deductions from operating expenses.
- **Non-GAAP Operating Expenses**: Adjusted operating expenses after excluding the specified impacts.

### 3. Key Trends, Peaks, and Notable Data Points:
- **GAAP Gross Margin**: Expected to be 74.8%.
- **Impact of Adjustments**: The adjustments are expected to reduce the gross margin by 0.2%, resulting in a Non-GAAP gross margin of 75.0%.
- **GAAP Operating Expenses**: Total operating expenses are projected at $6,650 million.
- **Stock-based Compensation Expense, Acquisition-related Costs, and Other Costs**: These are significant deductions totaling $1,650 million from the GAAP operating expenses.
- **Non-GAAP Operating Expenses**: After adjusting for the above mentioned costs, the operating expenses are projected at $5,000 million.

### 4. Time Period Covered:

### Type of Chart/Visualization:
The chart is a table format, presenting financial data across different fiscal periods.

### Metrics/Data Shown:
The table includes the following key metrics:
- **Diluted net income per share**: This metric is presented under two categories: GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) and Non-GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles excluding certain items). It shows the earnings per share for each fiscal period.
- **Weighted average shares used in diluted net income per share computation**: This indicates the number of shares used to compute the diluted net income per share for each fiscal period.
- **GAAP net cash provided by operating activities**: This represents the cash generated from core business operations during each fiscal period.
- **Purchases related to property and equipment and intangible assets**: This shows the amount spent on acquiring or improving fixed assets and intangible assets.
- **Principal payments on property and equipment and intangible assets**: This represents the payments made towards the principal of these assets.
- **Free cash flow**: This is calculated as the net cash provided by operating activities minus purchases related to property and equipment and intangible assets, plus principal payments on these assets.

### Key Trends, Peaks, and Notable Data Points:
1. **Diluted Net Income Per Share**:
   - The GAAP diluted net income per share fluctuates between $0.78 and $3.14.
   - The Non-GAAP diluted net income per share also fluctuates but generally follows a similar trend with values ranging from $0.81 to $3.16.
   - There are no significant peaks or troughs; the values remain relatively stable within a range.

2. **Weighted Average Shares Used**:
   - The weighted average shares used in the diluted net income per share computation range from 24,483 to 24,837.
   - This suggests a slight increase in the number of shares outstanding over the periods, indicating potential dilution or an increase in the company’s stock issuance.

3. **GAAP Net Cash Provided by Operating Activities**:
   - The cash provided by operating activities ranges from $15,365 to $66,530.
   - There is a noticeable peak in the fifth fiscal period at $66,530, which is significantly higher than the other periods.

4. **Purchases Related to Property and Equipment and Intangible Assets**:
   - These purchases range from $(813) to $(4,758).
   - The highest purchase amount is observed in the fifth fiscal period at $(4,758).

5. **Principal Payments on Property and Equipment and Intangible Assets**:
   - Principal payments range from $(29) to $(97).
   - The highest payment amount is seen in the fifth fiscal period at $(97).

6. **Free Cash Flow**:
   - Free cash flow ranges from $13,450 to $61,675.
   - The highest free cash flow is recorded in the fifth fiscal period at $61,675, which is significantly higher than the other periods.

### Time Period Covered:
The table covers five fiscal periods, although specific years are not mentioned. Each period is represented by a separate row.

### Year-over-Year Changes or Growth Rates:
- There is a noticeable year-over-year increase in the GAAP net cash provided by operating activities, particularly in the fifth fiscal period, where it reaches its peak at $66,530.
- The free cash flow also shows a significant increase in the fifth fiscal period, reaching $61,675, which is more than double the value in the fourth fiscal period.

Overall, the table highlights variations in financial performance across different fiscal periods, with a particular emphasis on the fifth fiscal period showing the highest levels of cash generation and free cash flow.

bullet_points: Revenue for the fourth quarter was a record \$68.1 billion,up 73% from a year ago and up 20% sequentially. Fiscal year revenue was a record \$215.9 bilion, up 65% from a year ago.

Data Center revenue for the fourth quarter was a record \$62.3 bilion, up 75% from a year ago and up 22% sequentialy,driven by the major platform shifts-accelerated computing and Al. For the fourth quarter, hyperscaler revenue increased and remained our largest customer category at slightly over 50% of Data Center revenue,while growth was led by the rest of our Data Center customers as revenue diversified.

Data Center compute revenue was a record \$51.3 billion,up 58% from a year ago and up 19% sequentially. Networking revenue was a record \$11.O bilion,up 263% from a year ago and up 34% sequentially from the introduction and continued ramp of NVLinkTM compute fabric for GB2O0 and GB300 systems and the growth of Ethernet and InfiniBand platforms.

Gaming revenue for the fourth quarter was up 47% from a year ago，driven by strong Blackwell demand. Gaming revenue was down l3% sequentially as channel inventory naturally moderated following a season of strong holiday demand. We expect supply constraints to be a headwind to Gaming in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and beyond.
Professional Visualization revenue for the fourth quarter was up 159% from a year ago and up 74% sequentially, driven by exceptional demand for Blackwell.
Automotive revenue for the fourth quarter was up 6% from a year ago and up 2% sequentialy, driven by continued adoption of our self-driving platforms.

GAAP operating expenses for the fourth quarter were up 45% from a year ago and up 16% sequentially，and non-GAAP operating expenses were up 51% from a year ago and up 21% sequentially. The fourth quarter GAAP increases from a year ago were driven by higher compensation and benefits expense due to employee growth,and compute and infrastructure costs.The non-GAAP increases were driven by compute and infrastructure costs and compensation and benefits.The fourth quarter GAAP and non-GAAP sequential increase was driven by engineering development materials for new product introductions and compute and infrastructure costs.

Interest income for the fourth quarter was \$568 million, up from a year ago and down sequentially, driven by changes in cash,cash equivalents,and debt securities.Net other income for the fourth quarter was \$5.6 bilion，driven by unrealized gains in non-marketable and publicly-held equity securities,including gains from our previously announced investment in Intel's common stock.

Cash,cash equivalents and marketable securities were \$62.6 billion, up from \$43.2 billion a year ago and \$60.6 billion a quarter ago. The increases primarily reflect higher revenue，partially offset by outlays for an intellectual property license, strategic investments and stock repurchases.
Accounts receivable was \$38.5 bilion with 51 days sales outstanding (DSO), down from 53 days sequentially, driven by timing of cash collections.

Inventory was \$21.4 billion,up from \$19.8 billon sequentiallyand total supply-related commitments were \$95.2 bilion. We have strategically secured inventory and capacity to meet demand beyond the next several quarters.
Multi-year cloud service agreements were \$27.0 billion,up from \$26.0 bilion sequentially,to support the growing needs of our research and development efforts.
Cash flow from operating activities was \$36.2 billion, up from \$16.6 billon a year ago and up from \$23.8 billion a quarter ago.The year-on-year and sequential increases reflect growth in revenue.

We returned \$4.1 bilion to shareholders in the fourth quarter through \$3.8 billion of share repurchases and \$243 million of cash dividends. In fiscal 2026，we returned \$41.1 billion to shareholders through \$40.1 billion of share repurchases and \$974 million of cash dividends.

Revenue is expected to be \$78.0 billion, plus or minus 2%. We are not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China in our outlook. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are expected to be 74.9% and 75.0%, respectively, plus or minus 50 basis points,inclusive of a 0.1% impact from stock-based compensation expense.
GAAP and non-GAAP operating expenses are expected to be approximately \$7.7 billon and \$7.5 billion, respectively, inclusive of \$1.9 billion of stock-based compensation expense.

To supplement NVIDIA's condensed consolidated financial statements presented in accordance with GAAP,the company uses non-GAAP measures of certain components of financial performance. These non-GAAP measures include non-GAAP gross profit， non-GAAP gross margin， non-GAAP operating expenses, non-GAAP operating income, non-GAAP other income (expense), net, non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP net income,or earnings,per diluted share,and free cash flow.For NVIDIA's investors to be better able to compare its current results with those of previous periods, the company has shown a reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP financial measures.The reconciliations for fiscal years 2O25 and 2026 adjust the related GAAP financial measures to exclude stock-based compensation expense,acquisition-related and other costs,other,gains/losses from non-marketable and publicly-held equity securities, net,interest expense related to amortization of debt discount, and the associated tax impact of these items where applicable. Beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2027，NVIDIA's non-GAAP financial measures will no longer exclude stock-based compensation expense.Free cash flow is calculated as GAAP net cash provided by operating activities less both purchases related to property and equipment and intangible assets and principal payments on property and equipment and intangible assets. NVIDIA believes the presentation of its non-GAAP financial measures enhances the user's overall understanding of the company's historical financial performance.The presentation of the company's non-GAAP financial measures is not meant to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the company's financial results prepared in accordance with GAAP,and the company's non-GAAP measures may be different from non-GAAP measures used by other companies.

revenue.description:
This is a financial table that provides quarterly financial performance data for a company over two fiscal years (FY26 and FY25). The data is presented in millions of dollars, except for earnings per share, which is expressed in dollars.

### 1. Type of Chart/Visualization:
The chart is a tabular representation of financial data, specifically a comparative financial statement table. It does not use any graphical elements like bars, lines, or pie charts but organizes the data in rows and columns for easy comparison.

### 2. Metrics/Data Shown:
The table includes the following financial metrics:
- **Revenue**: Total income from sales.
- **Gross Margin**: The percentage of revenue remaining after deducting the cost of goods sold.
- **Operating Expenses**: Costs related to running the business, excluding interest and taxes.
- **Operating Income**: Profit before interest and taxes.
- **Net Income**: Total profit after all expenses, including taxes.
- **Diluted Earnings per Share**: Net income divided by the weighted average number of shares outstanding during the period.

### 3. Key Trends, Peaks, and Notable Data Points:
- **Revenue Growth**: Revenue increased significantly from $39,331 million in Q4 FY25 to $68,127 million in Q4 FY26, marking a 73% increase year-over-year (Y/Y).
- **Gross Margin Improvement**: Gross margin improved slightly from 73.5% in Q4 FY25 to 75.2% in Q4 FY26, showing a 1.7 percentage point increase Y/Y.
- **Operating Expenses Increase**: Operating expenses rose from $3,378 million in Q4 FY25 to $5,102 million in Q4 FY26, indicating a 51% increase Y/Y.
- **Operating Income Growth**: Operating income grew substantially from $25,516 million in Q4 FY25 to $46,107 million in Q4 FY26, reflecting an 81% increase Y/Y.
- **Net Income Growth**: Net income also saw significant growth from $22,066 million in Q4 FY25 to $39,552 million in Q4 FY26, with a 79% increase Y/Y.
- **Earnings per Share Growth**: Diluted earnings per share increased from $0.89 in Q4 FY25 to $1.62 in Q4 FY26, showing a 82% increase Y/Y.

### 4. Time Period Covered:
The table covers the fourth quarter (Q4) of fiscal years 2026 (FY26) and 2025 (FY25).

### 5. Year-over-Year Changes or Growth Rates:
All key financial metrics show substantial growth Y/Y:
- Revenue: 73%
- Gross Margin: 1.7 percentage points
- Operating Expenses: 51%
- Operating Income: 81%
- Net Income: 79%
- Diluted Earnings per Share: 82%

These figures indicate strong financial performance and a significant improvement in profitability for the company over the given period.
